narrative.overview:
Gridec measures how an electrical network actually behaves and writes a conclusion a bank or a contractor can act on. The site is built as the first page of that document rather than as an advertisement for it. Warm paper carries a raking light and a trace of grain; ink plates turn over like the reverse of a sheet; numbers, counters and values are set in a pixel face because they come off an instrument, not out of a marketing department.

Restraint here is not a style preference — it is the credibility argument. In this market a quiet, exact page reads as competence, and a loud one reads as a sales operation with nothing measured behind it. So the accent appears only where something was actually measured, surfaces stay flat unless a sheet is genuinely lifted off the page, and every state change moves tone rather than shape.

The world is deliberately not a dark technical dashboard, a startup landing page with gradient headlines, or a card wall floating on soft shadows. Each was tried or proposed here and rejected.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with a directional light and 6 % grain — never a flat fill, never a cool grey
Hairlines instead of frames; 2 px radius everywhere
One blue, spent only on measured things
Pixel type for anything an instrument would print
Two languages on one type scale, matched by cap height rather than by point size
Depth by sheet order, not by shadow

rules.name: The Measured-Only Rule
rules.body: The brand blue marks something that was measured, counted or selected. If a proposed use cannot answer "what was measured here?", it is decoration and does not ship.

rules.name: The One Paper Rule
rules.body: There is a single light ground. When a light surface needs to feel different, change the light on it or the sheet it sits on — never introduce a second beige.

rules.name: The Warm Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on paper is #2B2722, not the plate ink. The plate ink on paper reads cold and pulls the page toward a screen; the warm ink keeps it a document.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Overused Grotesk speaks for the company; Departure Mono speaks for the instrument. The pixel face is allowed on numbers, counters, units, event labels and values — never on a sentence. On the Armenian page it is allowed on digits only: the font has zero Armenian glyphs.

rules.name: The Named-Step Rule
rules.body: New work uses a role from the ramp; a new size is drift until it earns a role. The system does not obey this everywhere yet: four overlay and card headings each invented their own size (enquiry dialog, photo dialog, contact call to action, invitation card), plus the success title and the close glyph. Resolving them onto Title and Headline is open work; adding a fifth is not.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: English and Armenian use the same headline ramp, number for number. Parity is judged by rendered cap height, not by point size.

rules.name: The Stack-Don't-Hide Rule
rules.body: A narrow screen may restack, reflow or re-letter a component, but may not remove content.

rules.name: The Paper-Layers Rule
rules.body: Depth equals the order of sheets. A sheet above another gets an edge; only a sheet actually lifted off the page gets a shadow.

rules.name: The Light-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: To make a light surface feel material, change the light on it — the raking gradient, the grain, a step of paper tone. Adding a soft drop shadow under a card is the rejected failure mode.

rules.name: The No-Dash, No-Circle Rule
rules.body: No dashed borders and no circular elements anywhere.

dos: Do spend the brand blue only on something measured, counted or selected — the Measured-Only Rule.
Do draw edges as box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px so hover and focus can change an edge without moving the layout.
Do keep one radius (2 px) and one easing curve (cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)) across every component; durations run 0.16 s for a press to 0.45 s for a ground change.
Do set numbers, units, counters and values in Departure Mono, and sentences in the text face.
Do change the English and Armenian type scales together, and verify parity by rendered cap height rather than by point size.
Do verify contrast numerically against WCAG AA, including composited alpha and gradient backdrops.
Do restack on narrow screens instead of hiding content.
donts: Don't add soft drop shadows under cards or panels to suggest depth.
Don't dim an element with opacity on a light ground — the paper shows through and becomes a white haze.
Don't use dashed borders or circular elements anywhere.
Don't introduce gradient text, coloured glow shadows or startup-style gradients.
Don't put a second beige on the page; there is one paper.
Don't use the plate ink for text on paper — text is warm ink.
Don't apply the pixel face to Armenian words; it has no Armenian glyphs.
Don't animate a keyboard-repeatable action, and don't let any UI transition exceed 0.6 s.
